brief_mapping:
You map one table from a scientific paper into a knowledge graph built from Pharos (the NIH Illuminating the Druggable Genome database) that follows the Biolink Model, version 4.4.3. A scientist gave the table with a description of the paper. You will be given the description, a card that describes the table (each column with its counts and its values or examples, and eight example rows), and the traits of the graph whose names match the disease the description names.

Propose how each row becomes one or more edges (associations) between a subject node and an object node. Code will check your proposal against the Biolink Model and against the data, and may send it back once with the reasons it was refused. Code sets each edge's date (the year the paper was published) and its knowledge source (the paper); do not give them.

Return ONE JSON object and nothing else, with these keys:

  "map": true, or false if this table should not become edges (then give only "map" and "reason")
  "subject": {"columns": [column, ...], "resolver": one of the resolvers below, "category": a Biolink class CURIE such as "biolink:Gene", "name_column": optional column that names the node, "separator": optional text that separates several values in one cell, each of which becomes its own edge}
  "object":  the same keys, or {"constant": one trait id from the list of traits, "category": a Biolink class CURIE} when every row's object is that one trait
  "predicate": a Biolink predicate CURIE, such as "biolink:related_to"
  "association_category": a Biolink association class CURIE, such as "biolink:Association"
  "knowledge_level": one of knowledge_assertion, logical_entailment, not_provided, observation, prediction, statistical_association
  "agent_type": one of automated_agent, computational_model, data_analysis_pipeline, image_processing_agent, manual_agent, manual_validation_of_automated_agent, not_provided, text_mining_agent
  "qualifiers": {} or {Biolink qualifier slot name: a constant value, or {"sign_of": column} for a direction qualifier}
  "edge_properties": [columns whose values the edge should carry]
  "keep_if": null, or {"column": c, "at_least": number, "reason": why a row below it is not asserted}, or {"column": c, "in": [values], "reason": ...}, or {"column": c, "matches": a regular expression, "reason": ...}. A row that fails it is kept as a recorded gap of its subject, not dropped, and needs no object.
  "split_by": null, or a column whose values need different mappings
  "by_value": only with split_by: {value: {any of subject, object, predicate, association_category, knowledge_level, agent_type, qualifiers, edge_properties, keep_if, given as overrides}, or {"skip": reason} to leave that value's rows out}
  "notes": up to 600 characters on the choices a reader might question

"columns" lists the columns to try in order; the first that gives an identifier is used.

RESOLVERS (code turns a cell into an identifier; you choose which):
  gene_symbol: the value is a gene symbol, such as APOE; gives every gene of the graph with that symbol (its Pharos symbol, or the Ensembl symbol of a gene the Pharos target is cross-referenced to). Graph genes are proteins here: use the category biolink:Protein
  curie: the value is already a compact identifier such as MONDO:0005148 (EFO_0004584 is read as EFO:0004584)
  prefix:P: the value is a local identifier under the prefix P, written P:<value> (for example prefix:NCBIGene)
  pattern:P:REGEX: the first group of the regular expression REGEX matched in the value, under the prefix P
  name:KIND: no identifier: a local node made from the text, marked as not grounded

Rules:
- Use only Biolink classes, predicates and qualifiers that exist in Biolink 4.4.3. The subject and object categories must fit the predicate's domain and range and the association class.
- Choose the most specific predicate the source supports, and no more specific than that.
- The knowledge level and agent type describe how the paper made the claim.
- Do not invent columns or values.

studies.what: The Alzheimer disease study, whose table had been built by hand before: do the stages reproduce it?
studies.description: Uffelmann et al. Alzheimer's disease genetics converges on microglial and neuronal dysregulation. Nature, published 28 October 2026. doi:10.1038/s41586-026-11206-y. Licence: CC BY-NC-ND 4.0. A genome-wide association study of Alzheimer's disease. Add the genes the study names at each associated locus.
studies.check_8: a row counts when its sides give identifiers of any kind, and 95% of rows must (ingest's check 8)

proposal.notes: SD2 lists the 127 loci from the multi-ancestry meta-analysis, with predicted effector gene(s) per locus in column 'Predicted effector gene(s)'. Header is on row 2. Rows 3-129 are data.

Each slash-separated gene in 'Predicted effector gene(s)' becomes its own edge to Alzheimer disease. These are the effector genes the paper predicts for each GWAS locus (via FLAMES and related methods), so the agent is a computational pipeline. Non-gene entries such as 'IGH gene cluster' and lncRNA-style names (e.g. AC008394.1) will not resolve to a graph protein and are left unmatched. Literature and Coloc_MR columns are not used, since they are literature or colocalisation candidates rather than the study's named effector genes. Direction of effect is not mapped as a qualifier.

studies.outcome: Reproduced: the model's mapping makes the same 181 pairs of a graph gene and Alzheimer disease as the table built by hand. It was compared, not joined, since the table built by hand is already beside the graph.

proposal.notes: Each lead variant row links its nearest protein-coding gene to Parkinson disease, as the paper names that gene at the locus.
